args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the v2.3.1 production deploy (error rate was 0.18 across us-east, us-west, and eu-west). Per the platform runbook, I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all production regions. Post-rollback status: all three regions on v2.3.0, healthy=true, error rate 0.002. v2.3.1 remains unhealthy in production and should not be redeployed until it is fixed. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Follow-up: investigate the v2.3.1 failure, and confirm checkout traffic and error rates are stable.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged the on-call engineer.

- **Why v2.3.0:** It is the most recent production release marked healthy. v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production, so I did not use it. Because v2.3.0 has already run healthy in production, no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Result:** Service status now shows v2.3.0 in every region, healthy, with the error rate down from 0.18 to 0.002.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 describes the v2.3.1 failure, the rollback, and the post-rollback status. It also notes that v2.3.1 should not be redeployed until it is fixed, and that v2.3.1-rc was unhealthy in staging.

Next steps for the on-call engineer are to investigate the v2.3.1 failure and confirm checkout traffic is stable.
